supplementaryReferences.title: Edible part and local use
supplementaryReferences.quote: Ripe purple-black berries are said to be edible
supplementaryReferences.note: SANBI qualifies the food statement; it is about ripe berries, not latex, bark or roots. Fruit presence February–September does not establish ripe picking throughout.

supplementaryReferences.title: Species identification in KwaZulu-Natal
supplementaryReferences.quote: they both contain black, berry-like edible fruits
supplementaryReferences.doc: University of KwaZulu-Natal, Phytochemical and elemental studies of two indigenous medicinal plants
supplementaryReferences.note: The primary study records confusion with Bridelia micrantha. It does not supply a safe harvest calendar or kg/tree.

care: Shelter this coastal tree from direct salt-laden sea wind; SANBI reports salt burn despite its coastal habitat.
purchase: Ask a nursery to confirm the species and lawful provenance. Check current collection requirements before taking plants or products from existing trees.
